summary: Interactive channel onboarding wizard with permission matrix and RBAC templates
description:
Issue summary:
We need a guided, interactive onboarding wizard for provisioning Slack channels (public/private), associated Jira project space stubs, and a templated Confluence page. The wizard should surface a permission matrix (who can join, who can post, archival schedule), pre-populated RBAC templates for common pod types, and automate service-account creation for channel apps/bots.

Impact:
Right now onboarding is manual and error-prone: channel creators often pick incorrect privacy settings, forget to add required compliance reviewers, or request overly broad permissions. This leads to follow-up tickets for access changes, intermittent security exposures, and a backlog in the internal-support queue. A self-service wizard reduces support load and shortens time-to-onboard for new pods.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Build a lightweight web-based wizard (hosted internally) reachable from the "New Channel" Confluence template and the Slack-provisioning bot.
- Step-driven UI: Purpose -> Visibility -> Membership policy -> App integrations -> Retention/archival policy -> Compliance reviewers -> Jira + Confluence stubs.
- Permission matrix must present recommended defaults per pod type and allow scoped overrides with justifications that record who approved.
- Provide 3 RBAC templates: Engineering Pod, Data Platform, External Partner. Templates map to Slack groups, Jira permissions scheme, and Confluence space permissions.
- Auto-create a dedicated service account and provision minimal bot scopes for each channel when integrations are selected; record keys in Vault.
- The wizard writes a structured record into Jira (INT-*) and optionally triggers a CLA/contract gating flow for external partner pods.
- All actions must produce audit log entries in Confluence page metadata and central audit log (security requirement).

Proposed flow / Steps to implement:
1) Design step flow and template matrix (Product + Support) — deliver mockups.
2) Prototype backend endpoints that call Slack Admin API, Jira project creation API, and Confluence REST API.
3) Integrate service-account creation with internal identity automation and secrets storage in Vault.
4) Implement approval step: For non-default broad permissions, wizard must require a named approver (group or user) and store approval as part of the Jira ticket.
5) Add an option to create a lightweight runbook stub (Confluence) with owner/slo/retention.
6) Create a small runbook and test plan for Support to use during rollout.

Risks / Privacy / Security notes:
- Creating automated service accounts increases attack surface; scopes must be principle-of-least-privilege and keys rotated on creation. Security to sign-off on scope list before implementation.
- External partner templates require additional gating to avoid data leakage — legal review required.

Dependencies:
- Slack Admin API permissions for provisioning (team-admin or org-integration role).
- Jira API token with project-creation rights or an internal provisioning service.
- Confluence template endpoints and a location for standardized templates.
- Vault secrets writer role for service-account keys.

Timeline suggestion:
- Week 1: finalize mockups & permission matrix with Security & Product.
- Week 2: backend prototype for Slack/Jira/Confluence calls; security review of service account scopes.
- Week 3: integrate approvals, vault storage, and audit logging.
- Week 4: internal pilot with two pods, iterate, then rollout.

investigation_notes: Reviewed last 30 support tickets tagged 'channel-provision' — average time-to-complete 3.8 days, ~48% required follow-up access changes.
Examined current automation repo: provisioning command only supports top-level creation; no integrated Confluence/Jira stubbing available.
Identified that Vault role for existing bot does not permit writing new service accounts without manual ops intervention — will need a short-lived elevated role or a provisioning lambda.
Security raised concern: some pods request full 'manage' permissions in Confluence; template needs to constrain to 'add' or 'edit' for specific groups only.

If approved, create two pilot channels: 'eng-runtime-pilot' and 'data-platform-pilot' and run the end-to-end flow including service-account creation and vault write.
